name: Action Simulation for Auditory Prediction (ASAP)
short_description: The motor system is recruited during beat perception because motor planning provides temporally precise predictions that auditory cortex alone cannot generate — beat perception is auditory-MOTOR from the outset
higher_order_principle: ASAP reframes auditory-motor interaction: the motor system does not passively respond to the beat — it actively generates the temporal predictions that constitute beat perception. Groove (the urge to move) is not a consequence of perceiving a beat; it IS the subjective experience of the motor prediction system being maximally engaged. The motor system evolved for precise timing; auditory cortex borrowed this precision for rhythm.

neural_substrate.dorsal_auditory_stream: Auditory cortex → parietal cortex → premotor cortex → SMA
neural_substrate.premotor_cortex: Generates motor plans (simulated movements at beat frequency)
neural_substrate.motor_cortex: Excitability fluctuates with beat — highest at expected beat times

asap_mechanism.prediction_source: Motor planning circuits, not auditory cortex
asap_mechanism.precision_advantage: Motor system evolved for precise timing; provides higher temporal precision than auditory processing alone
asap_mechanism.simulation: Motor system simulates movement at beat frequency even during passive listening

evolutionary_constraint.vocal_learning_hypothesis: Beat perception requires auditory-motor coupling that evolved for vocal learning
evolutionary_constraint.prediction: Beat perception in vocal learners (parrots ✓, songbirds — mixed), absent in non-vocal-learners (dogs, cats ✓)
evolutionary_constraint.exception: Sea lions — may use related but distinct pathway

causal_links.evidence_base: TMS to SMA impairs beat perception even without movement (Grube et al. 2010). Motor cortex excitability fluctuates with beat during passive listening (Stupacher et al. 2017).
Patel & Iversen (2014, ~500 citations): ASAP hypothesis. Motor simulation provides prediction; groove IS the phenomenology of this simulation.

scope_conditions: Applies to beat perception in periodic rhythms
Distinguishes beat perception (motor-dependent) from interval timing (cerebellar)
Predicts species distribution based on vocal learning capacity
moderators: Individual differences in dorsal auditory stream integrity
Age of training onset (sensitive period effects)

interactions.nature: M7 (BG) extracts periodicity; M10 (motor) provides precise temporal predictions
M11 describes how the auditory-motor connectivity underlying ASAP develops

key_references.citation: Patel, A. D., & Iversen, J. R. (2014). The evolutionary neuroscience of musical beat perception: The Action Simulation for Auditory Prediction (ASAP) hypothesis. Frontiers in Systems Neuroscience, 8, 57.
Patel, A. D. (2021). Vocal learning as a preadaptation for the evolution of human beat perception. Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B, 376(1835), 20200326.
Stupacher, J., Wood, G., & Witte, M. (2017). Synchrony and sympathy: Social entrainment with music. Psychomusicology, 27(3), 158-167.
